learning: Iteration 4 vs iteration 1 isolates the inertia effect: same sensors and controller, lower inertia gave slalom line loss 0.85 vs 0.1, and higher s-bend and oval progress. Test whether slalom line loss returns near 0.1 at mass 0.8 and body_length 0.18.
notes: Adopts the Builder's iteration-5 geometry, which reverts mass and body_length to the iteration-1 values, with the iteration-4 controller that scored best. Slalom line loss rose from 0.1 to 0.85 when inertia was lowered, so the inertia revert is the expected fix.
rationale: Iteration 4 (mass 0.7, body_length 0.14, y 0.03, kp 3.0, kd 0.3, base 1.2) scored 124.20, the best so far. Its slalom line loss was 0.85 per run. Iteration 1 used the same sensors and controller but mass 0.8 and body_length 0.18, and its slalom line loss was 0.1. Inertia is m(L^2+W^2)/12, so the reduced inertia is the most likely cause of the slalom line loss. The Builder's geometry for this iteration matches iteration 1 exactly (x = -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y 0.03, 16 mm footprints, mass 0.8, body_length 0.18), so I keep the controller that scored best in iteration 4. Its gains are kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.2, weights -2 to +2 and last_direction line loss. I am not retuning the controller here, because the only change that clearly helped was the lower inertia, and the lower inertia is what this geometry removes. The expected result is line loss near 0.1 on slalom and a score near iteration 1 (about 112), with s-bend and oval progress a little lower than in iteration 4. max_error has stayed at 0.063 m in every race, so it is not expected to move with these geometry values alone.
